title: Core Functions & Error Handling 🏗️
description: Implement backup, logging, disk checking, and robust error recovery – the backbone of the tool.

slides.title: Loading Configuration 🧾
slides.content:
## Reading key=value Safely

We'll use a `while read` loop with `IFS='='` to parse the config file, ignoring empty lines and comments.

```bash
while IFS='=' read -r key value; do
  [[ -z "$key" || "$key" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]] && continue
  key=$(echo "$key" | xargs)
  value=$(echo "$value" | xargs)
  declare -g "$key=$value"
done < "$CONFIG"
```
`declare -g` sets the variable globally (needed if inside function).

slides.title: Config Loader Function
slides.codeSnippet:
load_config() {
  while IFS='=' read -r key value; do
    [[ -z "$key" || "$key" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]] && continue
    key=$(echo "$key" | xargs)
    value=$(echo "$value" | xargs)
    declare -g "$key=$value"
  done < "$CONFIG"
}

quizData.question: Why use `declare -g` inside the config loading function?

options.text: To make variables local to the function
To ensure variables are available globally after the function ends
It's required for all variable assignments

quizData.explanation: Without `-g`, the `declare` would create a local variable (inside function). `-g` forces it into the global scope.

slides.title: Logging with Severity Levels 📝
slides.content:
## A Reusable `log` Function

We'll define `log INFO "message"`, `log ERROR "message"`. The function will:
- Prepend timestamp and level.
- Write to stdout (which can be redirected by cron to a file).
- Also append to a dedicated log file if `LOGFILE` is set.

```bash
log() {
  local level="$1"; shift
  local msg="[$(date +'%Y-%m-%d %T')] [$level] $*"
  echo "$msg"
  [ -n "${LOGFILE:-}" ] && echo "$msg" >> "$LOGFILE"
}
```

slides.title: Disk Space Check
slides.content:
Prevent backup if disk is too full:
```bash
check_disk() {
  local pct_used=$(df "$BACKUP_DEST" | awk 'NR==2 {print $5}' | tr -d '%')
  local free=$((100 - pct_used))
  if [ "$free" -lt "$THRESHOLD_PCT" ]; then
    log ERROR "Low disk space: ${free}% free, threshold ${THRESHOLD_PCT}%"
    send_alert "Backup aborted – low disk"
    exit 1
  fi
  log INFO "Disk space OK (${free}% free)"
}
```
slides.codeSnippet:
check_disk() {
  local pct_used=$(df "$1" | awk 'NR==2 {print $5}' | tr -d '%')
  local free=$((100 - pct_used))
  if [ "$free" -lt "${2:-10}" ]; then
    log ERROR "Low disk space: ${free}% free"
    return 1
  fi
  log INFO "Disk space OK: ${free}% free"
  return 0
}

quizData.question: The `df` command's `--output` option is the most portable way to get used percentage.
quizData.explanation: `--output` is a GNU extension; the `awk` method works on both GNU and BSD (macOS) `df`.

slides.title: The Backup Function 🗜️
slides.content:
## Create Compressed Archive

For each directory in `$BACKUP_SRC`:
- Use `tar -czf "$BACKUP_DEST/backup-$(hostname)-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).tar.gz" -C "$(dirname "$dir")" "$(basename "$dir")"`
- Handle errors: if tar fails, log and send alert.
- Use `||` to trigger failure action.

This preserves directory structure and compresses on the fly.

slides.title: do_backup Implementation
slides.codeSnippet:
do_backup() {
  for dir in $BACKUP_SRC; do
    local name="backup-$(hostname)-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).tar.gz"
    if tar -czf "$BACKUP_DEST/$name" -C "$(dirname "$dir")" "$(basename "$dir")"; then
      log INFO "Backed up $dir to $name"
    else
      log ERROR "Failed to backup $dir"
      send_alert "Backup failed for $dir"
      return 1
    fi
  done
}

slides.title: Rotating Old Backups 🧹
slides.content:
## Keep Only the Newest N

- List backup files by modification time (`ls -t`).
- Skip the first `$RETENTION` files (the newest).
- Delete the rest.

```bash
rotate_backups() {
  local files=($(ls -t "$BACKUP_DEST"/backup-*.tar.gz 2>/dev/null))
  for ((i=$RETENTION; i<${#files[@]}; i++)); do
    rm -f "${files[i]}" && log INFO "Rotated: removed ${files[i]}"
  done
}
```

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content: Test your rotation logic with a small retention number and dummy files before trusting it with real data.
